new_value: • Correct Statement (2): Archaeological finds confirm the worship of both female deities (abundant terracotta Mother Goddess figurines) and male deities (the 'Proto-Shiva' or Pashupati seal depicting a horned male figure surrounded by animals at Mohenjo-daro), as well as nature and tree worship (pipal). • Why Statement 1 is incorrect: Unlike ancient Egypt or Mesopotamia, no dedicated monumental temples, royal palaces, or dynastic tombs have ever been identified in any Indus Valley site; public architecture was civic and utilitarian (e.g., the Great Bath, granaries). • Why Statement 3 is incorrect: Horse-drawn chariots were introduced during the later Vedic period. Harappan transportation relied primarily on solid-wheeled bullock carts and pack animals; there is no evidence of horse-drawn chariots used in warfare. • Often confused with: The Rigvedic civilization, which was horse-centric, pastoral, and heavily utilized horse-drawn chariots (ratha) in battle, unlike the largely peaceful, commercial, and urban Harappans.
issues_found: Commonly confused because large Harappan structures (Citadel, Great Bath, Granaries) are mistaken for religious temples or royal palaces.
Candidates frequently conflate Rigvedic military technology (horse-drawn chariots) with the Indus Valley Civilization.
